title: The m row
cue: Close both lips for m, then open into the vowel. These are practice syllables, not five vocabulary words.

coaching.tongueAndLips: The tongue prepares for the next vowel; the lips make the closure.
coaching.airflow: Air passes through the nose during m.
coaching.speechExercise: Say mmm → ma, then me, mi, mo, mu. Open from the same light lip closure each time.
coaching.selfCheck: Keep the nasal m audible before the vowel.

title: The p row
cue: Close both lips, release, then say the vowel. Avoid a strong English-style puff of air.

coaching.tongueAndLips: The tongue prepares for the vowel. Keep the lip closure brief.
coaching.airflow: Briefly stop oral airflow, then release.
coaching.speechExercise: Say pa three times slowly, then pa → pi → pu. Feel the release with a hand in front of the mouth.
coaching.selfCheck: Use less aspiration than a strongly stressed English p; do not force a puff.

title: The t row
cue: Place the tongue tip against the back of the upper front teeth. Release into the vowel without a strong puff of air.

coaching.contactOrNarrowing: Tongue tip/blade at the upper front teeth
coaching.tongueAndLips: Use a light contact near the back of the upper teeth; release into the vowel.
coaching.speechExercise: Say ta → ti → tu slowly. Notice the dental contact rather than an English-style ridge contact.
coaching.selfCheck: Avoid a strong puff or an extra vowel after t.

title: The n row
cue: Let air pass through the nose for n, then move into the vowel.

coaching.contactOrNarrowing: Tongue tip at the ridge behind the upper front teeth
coaching.tongueAndLips: Make a light closure; prepare the next vowel without pressing hard.
coaching.airflow: Air passes through the nose during n.
coaching.speechExercise: Say nnn → na, then na → ni → nu. Release the tongue into each vowel.
coaching.selfCheck: Connected speech can move the contact place; that comes in the Core lessons.

title: The l row
cue: Touch the ridge behind the upper teeth with the tongue tip; let air pass around the sides.

coaching.contactOrNarrowing: Tongue tip near the ridge; sides leave space for airflow
coaching.tongueAndLips: Keep a light central tongue contact while air escapes at the sides.
coaching.airflow: Oral airflow around the sides of the tongue.
coaching.speechExercise: Say la → li → lu, then lado → lima → luna. Notice the vowel change without losing the l.
coaching.selfCheck: Do not add an extra vowel before the l.

title: The s row
cue: Make a continuous s, then move into the vowel. Later lessons introduce regional variation in syllable-final s.

coaching.contactOrNarrowing: Tongue approaches the ridge; a narrow channel remains
coaching.tongueAndLips: Do not seal the mouth; form a groove and leave space for airflow.
coaching.speechExercise: Say sss → sa, then sa → si → su. Keep the beginning continuous.
coaching.selfCheck: This is a narrowing target, not a complete contact. Syllable-final s varies regionally.

title: The /k/ sound row
cue: One sound, different spellings: c before a/o/u; qu before e/i. The u in que and qui is silent.

coaching.contactOrNarrowing: Back of tongue meets the soft palate, then releases
coaching.tongueAndLips: Keep the tongue tip relaxed while the tongue back closes and releases into the next vowel.
coaching.speechExercise: Say ka → ki → ku → ke → ko slowly. Start each vowel with a small tongue-back closure and release; avoid a large English-style puff.
coaching.selfCheck: Do not use the tongue tip for k. The closure location adjusts naturally with the vowel.

title: The /g/ sound row
cue: For this row, g before a/o/u and gu before e/i. The u in gue and gui is silent. Later practise softer g in connected speech.

coaching.contactOrNarrowing: Back of tongue at the soft palate; closure or narrowing depends on context
coaching.tongueAndLips: Start the hard-g row after a pause; later compare the more open gesture between vowels.
coaching.airflow: Stop or more open oral airflow, depending on context.
coaching.speechExercise: Say ga after a pause, then say mi gato. Compare the contextual beginning with a speaker model.
coaching.selfCheck: Use ga gue gui go gu for the hard-g sound family; ge and gi belong with j.

title: The ch row
cue: Begin with a brief closure and release into a ch sound. Practise the syllables, then use meaningful words.

coaching.contactOrNarrowing: Tongue blade just behind the ridge
coaching.tongueAndLips: Begin with a brief closure, then release into a narrow passage.
coaching.speechExercise: Say cha once, then cha → chi → chu. Keep closure and friction as one coordinated sound.
coaching.selfCheck: Do not separate it into two spoken syllables.

title: The f row
cue: Rest the lower lip lightly at the upper front teeth and let air flow through the narrow gap.

coaching.contactOrNarrowing: Upper front teeth near the lower lip
coaching.tongueAndLips: Leave a small opening instead of biting the lip.
coaching.airflow: Continuous oral airflow through the gap.
coaching.speechExercise: Say fff → fa, then fa → fi → fu with a gentle, continuous beginning.
coaching.selfCheck: Keep the lip contact light and the airflow steady.

title: B and v: the /b/ family
cue: Start after a pause with a gentle two-lip closure. Between vowels, Spanish often uses a more open lip gesture; b and v are not separate sound targets here.

coaching.contactOrNarrowing: Both lips; closure or narrowing depends on context
coaching.tongueAndLips: Keep lips light. Do not substitute upper-teeth-to-lower-lip English v.
coaching.airflow: A stop or a more open oral release, depending on context.
coaching.speechExercise: Say ba after a pause. Then compare la boca and a beber with a speaker model, noticing the lighter lip gesture within speech.
coaching.selfCheck: The letters b and v normally belong to the same sound family; contextual variants need their own examples.

title: The /d/ family
cue: Begin after a pause with the tongue near the back of the upper teeth. Between vowels the closure often becomes a light narrowing.

coaching.contactOrNarrowing: Tongue tip/blade near the upper front teeth
coaching.tongueAndLips: After a pause use a light closure. Between vowels, compare a more open gesture in a model phrase.
coaching.airflow: Closure or narrow oral passage, depending on context.
coaching.speechExercise: Say da after a pause, then cada día. Notice that the contact may be lighter within the phrase.
coaching.selfCheck: The sound can change with context without changing its written letter.

title: The single-tap r
cue: Use one quick tongue-tip contact near the ridge behind the upper teeth. These vowel-r-vowel patterns avoid teaching word-initial r as a tap.

coaching.contactOrNarrowing: One quick tongue-tip contact near the ridge
coaching.tongueAndLips: Keep the gesture brief and loose, then return to the vowel.
coaching.airflow: A very brief interruption in oral airflow.
coaching.speechExercise: Start with ara, then cara; compare cara and carro only after hearing clear models.
coaching.selfCheck: Use a vowel-r-vowel practice pattern; a word beginning with r normally uses the trill family.

title: Initial r and rr
cue: Let a relaxed tongue tip respond to airflow near the ridge. Build toward the trill gradually; pressing harder is not the goal.

coaching.contactOrNarrowing: Tongue tip near the ridge, with repeated vibration
coaching.tongueAndLips: Keep the tip relaxed and allow airflow to drive the vibration.
coaching.airflow: Oral airflow supports repeated brief tongue contacts.
coaching.speechExercise: Alternate a relaxed ra attempt with the word rama; pause between attempts. Use the model before adding speed.
coaching.selfCheck: A trill is not a tightly held tongue press. Mark it as developing if a clear trill is not yet available.

title: J and g before e/i
cue: Use a back-of-mouth narrowing with airflow. The degree and location of friction vary by region; some models use a lighter h-like sound.

coaching.tongueAndLips: For a velar model, raise the tongue back toward the soft palate without a complete seal.
coaching.airflow: Continuous airflow; friction can be stronger or lighter by region.
coaching.speechExercise: Say ja → ji → ju gently using the chosen model, then jamón → jirafa → jugo.
coaching.selfCheck: Do not force harsh throat friction; a lighter realization can be regional rather than an error.

title: Y and ll in a yeísta model
cue: Raise the front/body of the tongue toward the hard palate. The precise realization depends on context and region; yi uses an uncommon anchor word.

coaching.contactOrNarrowing: Tongue body approaches the hard palate
coaching.tongueAndLips: Follow the chosen regional model: constriction and friction vary.
coaching.airflow: Oral airflow with a region/context-specific constriction.
coaching.voicing: Usually voiced in the reference family; regional models differ
coaching.speechExercise: Say ya → yo → yu with one named speaker model, then yate → yo → yuca.
coaching.selfCheck: Do not mark valid Río de la Plata realizations or ll-preserving varieties as inherently wrong.

title: The ñ row
cue: Raise the tongue body toward the hard palate and let air flow through the nose; then release into the vowel.

coaching.contactOrNarrowing: Tongue body toward the hard palate
coaching.tongueAndLips: Use a palatal nasal gesture rather than a separate n plus an added syllable.
coaching.speechExercise: Say ña slowly, then ña → ñi → ñu; move into mañana and niño with a model.
coaching.selfCheck: The tongue-body target matters more than an English spelling approximation.
